key_insight: LuxAvatar combines an animatable 3D head representation with a neural shader to animate and relight a single portrait in real time. Separating geometry and reflectance from shading aims to preserve 3D control while capturing complex facial lighting.
problem_solved: Creating head avatars from one image that remain consistent across viewpoints, facial motion, and lighting changes—without sacrificing real-time performance.
method: Build an animatable 3D intrinsic Gaussian proxy that separates canonical geometry from reflectance attributes.
Deform and rasterize the Gaussians into physically based rendering (PBR) buffers consistent with viewpoint and motion.
Condition a causal autoregressive neural shader on these buffers to synthesize the final appearance.
impact: The approach could support interactive digital humans, virtual production, and telepresence with controllable lighting from minimal input. The supplied abstract is truncated, so quantitative performance and evaluation results are not available.

paper_title: LuxAvatar: Real-Time Relightable Head Avatars via Causal Neural Shading of 3D Intrinsic Proxies
paper_authors: Yipengjing Sun, Chenyang Wang, Boyao Zhou, Jiapeng Zhu, Ka Leong Cheng
